contentBlocks.title: Divyangjan Accommodation Privileges & Committee Mandate
paragraphs: The University enforces five statutory examination privileges for Divyangjan learners: (1) special coaching facilitation, (2) compensatory extra time for writing examinations, (3) dedicated separate examination room, (4) support of qualified scribes of the student's choice, and (5) customized question papers where required.

indicators.title: Anti-discrimination policy
indicators.subtitle: Institutional Equity, Anti-Harassment, and Anti-Ragging Frameworks

contentBlocks.text: Kristu Jayanti University operates a robust, multi-layered regulatory architecture ensuring zero tolerance towards discrimination, harassment, and ragging across all academic, administrative, and residential facilities.

contentBlocks.title: 1. Regulation for Promotion of Equity 2026 (UGC Regulations 2012)
paragraphs: Establishes a composite 9-member Equal Opportunity Cell (EOC) serving as Anti-Discrimination Cell, Gender Sensitisation Cell, and Disability Committee, chaired by the Director of Student Welfare with an Associate Director of Admissions as designated Anti-Discrimination Officer.

Strictly prohibits disclosing caste, religion, or disability status in classrooms, labelling learners as 'Reserved Category', derogatory remarks, differential evaluation, or denial of facilities. Enforces formal joint hearings within 15 days, orders within 7 days, appellate review by the EOC, and final review by the Vice Chancellor.

contentBlocks.title: 2. Prevention of Sexual Harassment Regulations 2026 (UGC Regulations 2015)
paragraphs: Enforces zero tolerance across campuses, hostels, transit, and events. An Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) is chaired by a Senior Woman Professor with 50%+ female representation, faculty, staff, student nominees, and an independent external NGO representative.

Select Committee verifies complaints within 7 working days, completes enquiries within 45 days, mandates confidentiality under Section 16 of the POSH Act 2013, and provides interim protection and medical/counselling relief.

contentBlocks.title: 3. Regulation for Prevention and Control of Ragging (Revised) 2026
paragraphs: Implements zero tolerance under Supreme Court directives and UGC Regulations 2009. Governed by the Anti-Ragging Committee (ARC) chaired by the Vice Chancellor with civil/police representation, media, NGOs, parents, faculty, and students.

Supported by an Anti-Ragging Squad (ARS) conducting surprise inspections of hostels and campus areas, mandatory 10-student mentoring groups in every class, and statutory FIR lodgement within 24 hours for cognizable offences.

indicators.text: 10.6.7 Accessible facilities for persons with disabilities
indicators.subtitle: Physical and Digital Barrier-Free Campus Infrastructure

contentBlocks.text: The University continuously improves physical and digital infrastructure to ensure barrier-free mobility and accessible learning environments for individuals with disabilities.

Campus developments feature wheelchair-accessible ramps with handrails, passenger lifts equipped with audio announcements, dedicated accessible restrooms, reserved seating in auditoriums, and assistive technologies in library learning spaces.

contentBlocks.text: The Jayantian Determination Scholarship (JDS) provides recurring financial support to eligible disabled students across undergraduate and postgraduate programmes, ensuring economic barriers do not impede higher education access.

The Disability Accommodation (Divyangjan) Policy outlines institutional procedures for evaluating accommodation requests, allocating assistive equipment, and overseeing reasonable adjustments in classroom instruction and evaluations.

The policy mandates periodic reviews by the Disability Accommodation Committee in consultation with the Equal Opportunity Cell, ensuring that all physical and digital services comply with the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act.
